gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The director, ___ we met at the conference, has written to us.
gaps.hint: person as object, but the clause is non-defining
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses 'that' cannot replace 'who', even when the person is the object.

gaps.sentence: Have you got anything ___ will remove this stain?
gaps.explanation: After 'anything', 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun; 'which' is avoided after -thing words.

gaps.sentence: The people ___ moved in upstairs are very quiet.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' is the subject relative pronoun for people; 'whose' would need a noun after it.

gaps.sentence: His latest film, ___ was shot entirely in Iceland, won three awards.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is the subject pronoun for the film; 'that' never appears in non-defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: That's the office ___ I worked for ten years.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' means 'in which'; 'I worked the office' shows the place role of the gap.

gaps.sentence: The police have arrested the man ___ stole the painting.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' is the subject relative pronoun for people in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.
